draft.title: Tsarist autocracy
card: Autocracy is rule by one person whose power is not limited by a parliament or a constitution. In Russia this person was the tsar.
Nicholas II became tsar in 1894. Until 1905 he had no parliament to share power with, and he held that his right to rule came from God.
The army put down protests and strikes. The Orthodox Church taught that obeying the tsar was a religious duty.
The Okhrana, the secret police, watched critics and arrested them. Censorship also limited what people could read and say.
draft.remember: The tsar's power rested on force and belief: the army, the Okhrana, and the Church.

a.q: Which description best fits the tsar's rule in Russia under Nicholas II?
opts: One ruler whose power had no legal limit
One ruler whose power was checked by an elected body
A ruler chosen by the army to serve for a set term
A ruler who shared power equally with the Church
a.why: Autocracy means one person holds power that no parliament or constitution limits. Nicholas II had no parliament before 1905, so his power was not checked by an elected body. The Church supported him but did not share power with him.
a.clue: Think about who could limit the tsar's decisions.

b.q: A Russian priest in 1900 tells his village that disobeying the tsar is a sin. Which support for the tsar's rule does this show?
opts: The Church teaching obedience as a religious duty
The Okhrana watching and arresting critics
The army putting down protests by force
Censorship limiting what people could read
b.why: The priest speaks for the Orthodox Church, which taught that obeying the tsar was a religious duty. The Okhrana and the army used watching and force, not religious teaching. Censorship limited what people could read, not what they believed was a sin.
b.clue: Look at who is speaking and what kind of authority they use.

a.best: One ruler whose power had no legal limit

b.best: The Church teaching obedience as a religious duty

problems.detail: The remember line sorts the supports into 'force' (army, Okhrana) and 'belief' (Church), a split the card never makes. It also leaves out censorship and divine right, which the card teaches as part of the tsar's power.

The question asks about Nicholas II's rule as a whole (1894–1917). The card itself says he had no parliament only until 1905, and after 1906 the Duma and the Fundamental Laws set some formal limits. 'No legal limit' is clearly the best answer, but naming a timeframe such as 'before 1905' would avoid any doubt.
